claims.support: The evidence provides ranked data for 151 mapped countries and territories under indicator SN.ITK.SVFI.ZS representing Severe Food Insecurity.
The indicator measures severe food insecurity rates across the mapped universe.

claims.text: A documentary-style look at global food insecurity, comparing the zero-percent rates of Indonesia and Italy to the extreme hunger in South Sudan.
claims.support: Indonesia (IDN) is 0.0% (rank 144), Italy (ITA) is 0.0% (rank 144), and South Sudan (SSD) is 62.9% (rank 1).

claims.text: Indonesia reports 0% severe food insecurity. In South Sudan, it is 62.9%.

claims.text: This counts households forced to skip meals or go whole days without eating due to a lack of money.
claims.support: Definition matches: 'A household is classified as severely food insecure when at least one adult in the household has reported to have been exposed... to have skipped meals... or having to go for a whole day without eating because of a lack of money or other resources.'
